items.headline: Greed rebounds to 87 while valuation remains extreme at 85
items.summary: The 22 August AGCI snapshot records Greed at 87/100, up 5 points daily, while Valuation remains 85/100. Regime is Mid Bull, confidence 73/100 and the matrix remains EUPHORIA_RISK — Capital preservation / Do not chase.
items.whyItMatters: The prior cooling in sentiment did not persist. With valuation still extreme, the rebound in risk appetite argues against broad beta chasing and supports maintaining deployable liquidity for better entry terrain.
items.agciSignal: GREED REBOUNDS / VALUATION STILL EXTREME / PRESERVE LIQUIDITY

items.headline: Iran grants selective Hormuz passage to Iraqi oil tankers while broader disruption persists
items.summary: Iran granted special permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad. Traffic remains far below pre-war norms and the strait continues to be a high-risk route.
items.whyItMatters: Selective exemptions reduce immediate stress for some Iraqi barrels but do not normalize the chokepoint. AGCI treats this as evidence that energy flows remain policy-dependent and vulnerable to sudden disruption.
items.agciSignal: SELECTIVE RELIEF / STRUCTURAL HORMUZ RISK REMAINS

items.headline: Washington prepares new Iran sanctions with China exposure in focus
items.summary: The United States plans to announce new Iran sanctions on 24 August while signaling pressure on major trading partners, including China. Oil traffic through Hormuz remains severely impaired despite limited exemptions.
items.whyItMatters: The next sanctions package could broaden the shock from shipping to trade finance, Chinese demand channels and secondary-sanctions risk. That keeps an upside tail on oil and inflation even without renewed direct military escalation.
items.agciSignal: SANCTIONS ESCALATION RISK / ENERGY-INFLATION TAIL STAYS ELEVATED

items.headline: AI-linked U.S. manufacturing revival becomes a new stock-selection theme
items.summary: Barron's new 22 August magazine edition highlights a possible U.S. manufacturing revival supported by AI investment and reshoring, alongside renewed attention to industrial names, preferred securities and valuation-sensitive opportunities after the bond selloff.
items.whyItMatters: AGCI treats the theme as a diversification opportunity away from pure software and semiconductor beta. The key filter is whether industrial beneficiaries have durable order books, pricing power and acceptable leverage under a high long-rate regime.
items.agciSignal: RESHORING + AI CAPEX / SELECT INDUSTRIALS OVER BROAD BETA

items.headline: Mexico expects U.S. trade outcomes to track emerging Canada framework
items.summary: Mexico's economy minister said Mexico expects trade understandings with the United States similar in important respects to the emerging U.S.-Canada framework. Talks continue on steel, aluminum and North American supply chains, while more complex auto rules and labor issues may extend into 2027.
items.whyItMatters: This is a modest positive for Mexican manufacturing and nearshoring because it reduces the probability of Mexico being isolated from a broader North American framework. It does not eliminate headline risk or the possibility of sector-specific tariffs.
items.agciSignal: USMCA PATH IMPROVES MARGINALLY / NEARSHORING THESIS INTACT

items.headline: Nvidia expands infrastructure exposure ahead of 26 August earnings
items.summary: Nvidia made a minority investment in data-center developer Cloverleaf Infrastructure, reinforcing its strategy to accelerate U.S. AI data-center buildout. The move arrives ahead of Nvidia's 26 August earnings report and amid rising scrutiny of AI financing intensity.
items.whyItMatters: The AI cycle is expanding from chips into power, sites and financing. AGCI remains constructive on structural demand but raises the hurdle rate for projects dependent on external capital while long Treasury yields remain elevated.
items.agciSignal: AI INFRASTRUCTURE BROADENS / WATCH RETURNS ON CAPITAL AND FINANCING
